This is the staged path through **OrgMod**, the modernization member of the
Org family — migration without rip-and-replace, governed by the same spine.
Each stage names what to **read**, what to **do**, and how to **verify**.
The path invents nothing: every stage sequences material that is already
published, per [ADR-131](../adr/adr-131-academy-org-family-umbrella.qmd).
The pillar's front door is the [OrgMod landing](../orgmod/index.qmd).

As on every path: keep [Substrate Status](../docs/substrate-status.qmd)
open. It is the candid map of what is implemented, partial, and
aspirational.

---

## Stage 1 — The arc (where are we going?)

**Read:** [Microsoft Client-Server to Hybrid-Cloud Transformation](../customer-documents/operational-guides/client-server-to-hybrid-cloud/index.qmd)
— the eleven-chapter narrative that answers the big question: *we have an
AD forest; where are we going, how do we get there, and what does the
finished state look like?* Its crosswalk maps eleven AD-era dependencies
(identity, GPO, DNS, DHCP, PKI, RADIUS, LDAP, replication, time,
SYSVOL) to their hybrid-cloud targets.

**Do:** for your own estate, mark each of the eleven dependencies as
present / absent / already migrated.

**Verify:** you can name, for any dependency you marked present, its
target surface and why the arc sequences it where it does.

## Stage 2 — The bridge (what replaces AD's implicit roles?)

**Read:** [Directory Migration — the AD infrastructure bridge](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/directory-migration.qmd),
then the [eight adapter interfaces](../customer-documents/operational-guides/directory-migration/index.qmd)
behind it. AD was never just a directory — it was the implicit substrate
for addressing, authentication, naming, and policy; the bridge makes each
implicit role explicit before anything replaces it.

**Do:** for one adapter interface, write down what your estate uses today
to fill that role and what the target surface is.

**Verify:** you can explain why "migrate the directory" understates the
problem — and what breaks first when the implicit roles are ignored.

## Stage 3 — The planes (endpoints and servers)

**Read:** [Intune + Azure Arc Modernization](../customer-documents/operational-guides/intune-arc-modernization/index.qmd)
— the device- and server-plane workstream, runnable **two ways from the
same scripts**: a manual path (`-WhatIf` previews under local change
control) and a UIAO/OrgPath-governed path (every change bound to an
organizational path, an actuation rung, and a recorded approval).

**Do:** run the manual path's preview steps against a test scope; then
read the governed path and identify what the governance adds to each of
the same steps.

**Verify:** you can state why building the manual path first loses
nothing — the governed path binds the same scripts rather than replacing
them.

## Stage 4 — The identity pipe (HR-driven joiner/mover/leaver)

**Read:** the [HRIT to HR-Driven IAM Execution Plan](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/OrgComp_HRIT_HR_Driven_IAM_Execution_Plan.qmd)
— the provisioning pipeline from the federal HR source of truth to the
directory, on the program's wave clock. Then the
[Day-2 operations kit](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/OrgComp_Day2_Kit_0_Start_Here.qmd),
which ships **two editions**: a Current State edition for today's
hybrid AD-mastered estate, and a Target edition for the cloud-native
end state.

**Do:** trace one mover event from the HR record through to the
directory attribute change and its closure evidence, in whichever
edition matches your estate.

**Verify:** you can explain why the HR system — not the directory — is
where an identity change originates, and what the wave clock means for
sequencing your own rollout.

## Stage 5 — A worked consumer (proof at estate scale)

**Read:** the [SQL Server Identity Transformation](../customer-documents/sql-server-narrative/index.qmd)
series — a twenty-year SQL estate migrated off Windows Authentication onto
Entra ID, end to end. This is the pattern for any consumer workload that
inherited AD assumptions.

**Do:** pick one workload in your own estate that authenticates the old
way and outline its equivalent of the series' migration stages.

**Verify:** you can name where your workload's migration would land on the
addressing plane OrgPath governs, and what evidence of the change OrgComp
would prove.

## The law, at migration scale

Every wave on this path is a batch of MACD-R Moves: originated by the
modernization plan's source of truth, executed under just-in-time roles,
each emitting per-object closure evidence — an audited operation, not a
weekend of standing admin rights. Read
[One lifecycle, three pillars](../orgmod/index.qmd#macdr) and the full
doctrine in
[OrgComp Vol 0 Book 00](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd#macdr-lifecycle).

## Where this path leads

The full task-oriented shelf is
[Modernization guides](../customer-documents/operational-guides/index.qmd)
— the transformation engine, target surface, and program-management
discipline. If your next step is governing the estate you just modernized,
continue to the [OrgPath path](orgpath-path.qmd); if it is proving the
estate to an authorizing official, continue to the
[OrgComp Training Program](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/OrgComp-Training-Program/index.qmd).
